cards.title: Indexes start at 0
cards.body: Each character in a string has a position called an index. The first is at `[0]`, the second at `[1]`.

hi.title: Indexes 0 se shuru hote hain
hi.body: String ke har character ki ek position hoti hai jise index kehte hain. Pehla `[0]` par hai, doosra `[1]` par.

cards.title: Negative indexes count from the end
cards.body: `[-1]` is the last character, `[-2]` the one before it.

hi.title: Negative indexes end se ginte hain
hi.body: `[-1]` aakhri character hai, `[-2]` usse pehle wala.

cards.title: len() gives the length
cards.body: `len(word)` counts the characters. The last index is always `len(word) - 1`.

hi.title: len() length deta hai
hi.body: `len(word)` characters ginta hai. Aakhri index hamesha `len(word) - 1` hota hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: It should print the last letter, `n`, but crashes with an `IndexError`. Tap the bug.

bug.fix: Indexes start at 0, so the last one is `len(word) - 1`. The short way is `word[-1]`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: Isse aakhri letter `n` print karna chahiye, par yeh `IndexError` dekar crash hota hai. Bug par tap karo.
hi.fix: Indexes 0 se shuru hote hain, isliye aakhri `len(word) - 1` hai. Chhota tareeka hai `word[-1]`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: Index 1 is the second letter, y. Index -2 is the second from the end, o.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: Index 1 doosra letter hai, y. Index -2 end se doosra hai, o.

exercise.prompt: Read a word and print its first letter and its last letter, separated by a space. Use indexes `[0]` and `[-1]`.
exercise.promptHi: Ek word padho aur uska pehla aur aakhri letter print karo, beech mein ek space. Indexes `[0]` aur `[-1]` use karo.
exercise.starterCode:
word = input()
# print the first and last letters
